target_frame.title: Intermittent cold-room delivery gaps
target_frame.problem: A regional food distributor finds that some refrigerated deliveries arrive above its internal receiving temperature range, although the loading records show acceptable temperatures. The operations manager must decide what to investigate next and which temporary handling changes are justified before the next fortnight of deliveries.
known_context: There are three loading bays, two contracted carriers and routes lasting between forty minutes and four hours.
Drivers record departure and arrival times; receiving staff take a single temperature reading from one package per delivery.
Loading-bay logs record room temperature every fifteen minutes, but packages are not individually tracked between staging and loading.
The recent exceptions occur on both short and long routes. Receiving methods differ between customer sites.
A small pool of reusable temperature loggers is available, but the team cannot instrument every package or cancel routine deliveries.
target_frame.uncertainty: The manager does not know whether the exceptions mainly arise before loading, in transit, during receiving, or from differences in measurement. Multiple contributors may be present.
target_frame.decision_need: Identify a feasible investigation and defensible interim action without claiming that the existing endpoint records locate the cause.
constraints: Normal food-handling requirements remain in force.
Staff can add limited observations for two weeks; there is no budget for fleet replacement.

source_instrument.state: Several plausible explanations can account for an uncertain situation, and available evidence may fit more than one of them.
source_instrument.operation: State the competing explanations explicitly, evaluate each item of evidence against all of them, emphasize evidence that is inconsistent with particular explanations, and test the sensitivity of the resulting comparison to uncertain evidence or assumptions.
source_instrument.signal: The evidence forms a comparative pattern of consistency and inconsistency across the competing explanations, with some items discriminating among them more strongly than others.
source_instrument.inference: Explanations with greater important inconsistency can be weakened or eliminated, leaving a smaller set of alternatives that better survives the observed evidence.
source_instrument.limit: Missing hypotheses, dependent or unreliable evidence, subjective consistency judgments, poor assessment of diagnosticity, and shared assumptions can make the comparison misleading. Surviving contradiction is not proof that the remaining explanation is true.

S001.text: Several plausible explanations can account for an uncertain situation, and available evidence may fit more than one of them.

S002.text: State the competing explanations explicitly, evaluate each item of evidence against all of them, emphasize evidence that is inconsistent with particular explanations, and test the sensitivity of the resulting comparison to uncertain evidence or assumptions.

S003.text: The evidence forms a comparative pattern of consistency and inconsistency across the competing explanations, with some items discriminating among them more strongly than others.

S004.text: Explanations with greater important inconsistency can be weakened or eliminated, leaving a smaller set of alternatives that better survives the observed evidence.

S005.text: Missing hypotheses, dependent or unreliable evidence, subjective consistency judgments, poor assessment of diagnosticity, and shared assumptions can make the comparison misleading.

S006.text: Surviving contradiction is not proof that the remaining explanation is true.

P001.text: Investigate four competing explanations: warming during staging/loading, warming in transit, warming during receiving, and differences or errors in measurement.

P002.text: Include combinations; these mechanisms need not be mutually exclusive.

P003.text: Existing bay temperatures and single-package arrival readings do not establish package temperatures throughout the journey or locate a cause.

P004.text: Assume provisionally that loggers can be deployed safely and linked to selected packages; verify this before starting.

P005.text: For two weeks, rotate the available loggers across selected deliveries covering all three bays, both carriers, short and long routes, and different receiving sites where feasible.

P006.text: Include deliveries with and without prior exceptions; record coverage gaps.

P007.text: Identify monitored packages from staging through receipt, synchronize clocks, and record staging, loading, departure, arrival, unloading and receiving-measurement times.

P008.text: Record logger placement and whether it measures package temperature or surrounding air; do not equate these.

P009.text: Check logger and receiving-device performance using approved procedures.

P010.text: At receipt, pair the site's usual reading with a consistent, approved measurement on the tracked package where feasible, documenting method, location and delay without compromising handling.

P011.text: Before reviewing results, write predictions for each explanation.

P012.text: Build an evidence-by-explanation table marking consistency, inconsistency or indeterminate, with reasons and confidence.

P013.text: Evaluate every observation against every explanation, including combined explanations; prioritize reliable contradictions over counts of supporting observations.

P014.text: Repeat the comparison after excluding unreliable readings, treating observations from one delivery as dependent, varying uncertain handoff times and sensor-response assumptions, and separating air from package measurements.

P015.text: Review exceptions promptly and the full comparison at fortnight's end.

P016.text: Stop using a device or procedure if it compromises food handling; flag failed or missing traces as inconclusive and redeploy safely.

P017.text: Look for time-localized changes and paired-measurement agreement.

P018.text: A reliable package-relevant rise before loading, followed by stable transit readings, would contradict transit as the sole origin for that monitored package.

P019.text: Acceptable conditions through departure followed by a transit rise would weaken a solely preloading explanation.

P020.text: Acceptable conditions through arrival followed by warming during documented receiving delay would weaken explanations confined to earlier stages.

P021.text: Disagreement between usual and standardized readings would support investigating measurement differences, while agreement on elevated package temperature would weaken measurement differences as the sole explanation.

P022.text: These comparisons require adequate temporal resolution, suitable sensor placement and comparable measurements; otherwise mark the evidence indeterminate.

P023.text: Multiple rises could support combined contributors.

P024.text: No such observations are yet established.

P025.text: Weaken explanations in proportion to the importance and reliability of their contradictions, eliminating one only within the scope actually tested.

P026.text: Direct the next investigation toward alternatives that survive and observations that would distinguish them.

P027.text: During the fortnight, reinforce existing cold-staging practices, reduce avoidable unprotected handoff delays, and standardize approved receiving measurements where feasible.

P028.text: Use credible stage-specific evidence to target additional temporary supervision or handling changes at that stage.

P029.text: Apply existing food-handling and disposition requirements whenever a reading triggers them; do not await causal certainty or relax requirements.

P030.text: At fortnight's end, retain justified temporary controls and, if the ranking remains unstable or coverage inadequate, specify a focused next sampling round rather than declare a cause.

P031.text: Sparse, selectively monitored packages cannot establish prevalence or clear an entire delivery, carrier, bay or route.

P032.text: Air traces, sensor lag, clock errors, device error, package variability and different measurement locations can create misleading apparent contradictions.

P033.text: Repeated readings and records from one delivery are not independent confirmations.

P034.text: Missing mechanisms, subjective consistency judgments, mistaken diagnosticity and shared assumptions may distort every comparison; sensitivity to these requires an explicitly uncertain conclusion and revised hypotheses or measurements.

P035.text: An internal-range exception alone does not establish food-safety status.

P036.text: Surviving contradiction does not prove an explanation true, and improvement after a temporary change does not by itself establish causation.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Warming during staging/loading, warming in transit, warming during receiving, and measurement differences or errors are competing explanations to investigate.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 explicitly identifies uncertainty about preloading, transit, receiving, and measurement contributions. The proposition faithfully restates these as candidate explanations to investigate, preserving uncertainty without asserting that any occurred or that the set is exhaustive.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Warming during staging/loading, warming in transit, warming during receiving, and measurement differences or errors are competing explanations to investigate.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Explicitly identifying these candidates instantiates the source mechanism's hypothesis-formulation step. The target's untracked preloading interval, uncertain transit and receiving contributions, and differing measurement methods justify investigating these alternatives. This structures a relevant comparison without asserting that any candidate is established, mutually exclusive, or exhaustive; it does not establish that testing has occurred or located a cause.

obligation_verdicts.subject: The proposed mechanisms need not be mutually exclusive, so combined explanations belong in the comparison.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 explicitly allows multiple contributors. Including combined explanations faithfully applies S002's comparison of evidence across competing explanations and addresses S005's concern about missing hypotheses. This makes the investigation relevant to potentially overlapping causes without asserting that any particular combination has occurred or that the comparison has already produced results.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Existing bay temperatures and single-package arrival readings do not establish package temperatures throughout the journey.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 describes room-temperature logs at fifteen-minute intervals, no individual package tracking between staging and loading, and one package reading per delivery at receipt. These records lack package-specific temperature coverage across the journey. Even accurate endpoint readings and bay logs cannot establish the intervening package temperatures, justifying the limitation at its stated scope and strength.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Safe logger deployment is a provisional assumption that must be verified before starting.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule has a determinate prospective trigger—before starting the investigation—and a prescribed response: verify safe logger deployment before proceeding. This prerequisite is internally coherent with continuing normal food-handling requirements. Unspecified verification methods do not defeat this sequencing rule; the judgment does not establish that safe deployment is feasible or has been verified.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Provisional feasibility of safe logger deployment
unresolved_conditions: Verify before starting that the available loggers can be deployed without compromising applicable food-handling requirements.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 establishes logger availability, but not safe deployability. P004 explicitly makes feasibility a provisional assumption requiring verification; it supplies no observation establishing safety. The assertion is supportable only with that condition unresolved, not as confirmed feasibility.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Verify safe logger deployment
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Checking deployment safety is relevant to the target's food-handling constraint, but this prerequisite does not instantiate the transferred mechanism of comparing competing explanations, emphasizing contradictions, and testing sensitivity. No verification procedure connects this check to that mechanism. The proposal therefore fails this operation contract; this does not establish that logger deployment is unsafe.

obligation_verdicts.subject: The ability to link loggers to selected packages is a provisional assumption that must be verified before starting.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule establishes a coherent prospective prerequisite: before starting the investigation, verify that loggers can be linked to selected packages. Its timing and required response are sufficiently determinate for package-attribution governance. Unspecified linkage methods and reliability criteria do not defeat that decision structure. This judgment does not establish that linkage is feasible or has been verified.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Provisional feasibility of linking loggers to selected packages
unresolved_conditions: Verify before starting that logger records can be reliably attributed to the selected packages throughout the monitored journey.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 establishes logger availability but no existing individual package tracking between staging and loading. P004 explicitly leaves linkage as an assumption requiring verification; it does not demonstrate feasibility. The assertion is defensible only provisionally, with package attribution unresolved.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Verify logger-to-package linkage
unresolved_conditions: Specify a feasible linkage check and acceptance criteria that establish reliable attribution of logger records to selected packages throughout the monitored stages.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Checking attribution supports reliable evidence comparison and addresses the target's missing package tracking. It is a prerequisite to the transferred comparison, not itself a diagnostic comparison. The unspecified method and acceptance criteria leave its adequacy unresolved; the proposal does not establish successful linkage.

obligation_verdicts.subject: The proposed investigation uses a two-week rotation of available loggers across selected deliveries spanning all three bays, both carriers, short and long routes, and different receiving sites where feasible, including deliveries with and without prior exceptions and recording coverage gaps.
unresolved_conditions: A workable rotation must fit the available loggers, staff capacity and two-week window, with achievable coverage documented.
Safe deployment and reliable package attribution must be verified, and measurements must be sufficiently comparable and time-resolved to inform the competing explanations.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The target's operational diversity and limited logger pool justify selective rotation as a relevant evidence-gathering design. Including deliveries with and without prior exceptions creates opportunities for comparisons consistent with the source mechanism. However, coverage alone does not establish diagnosticity: feasibility and interpretable measurements remain unresolved. The proposal establishes neither successful sampling nor causal findings, and supports no claim of representativeness.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Measurements of surrounding air and measurements of package temperature must not be equated and should remain separate in the comparison.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Air and package temperatures measure distinct physical quantities and can differ because packages respond to ambient changes over time. The target's room-temperature logs therefore cannot substitute directly for package measurements. Preserving this distinction in comparisons and sensitivity checks is justified by the risk of misleading consistency judgments. This does not preclude air measurements providing indirect evidence or assert that a discrepancy has been observed.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Where feasible and without compromising handling, the proposed receipt comparison pairs the site's usual reading with a consistent, approved measurement on the tracked package, documenting method, location, and delay.
unresolved_conditions: An approved measurement method must be feasible within staffing and food-handling constraints.
Package linkage, measurement reliability, and acceptable timing and location differences must be established so the paired readings are interpretable.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The target explicitly includes differing receiving methods and uncertainty about measurement contributions. A paired comparison can supply relevant evidence for comparing explanations, consistent with the source mechanism. Documenting method, location, and delay helps assess alternative reasons for disagreement. However, the packet does not establish the approved method or acceptable pairing tolerances. Without these, differences could reflect package variation or intervening warming rather than measurement effects. The proposal therefore has conditional diagnostic warrant; its presence does not establish successful execution or any observed result.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Predictions for each explanation should be written before reviewing the results.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Writing predictions in advance provides explicit expectations against which later observations can be assessed for consistency and contradiction, faithfully supporting S002's comparative operation. This is relevant to distinguishing the target's unresolved explanations. The source does not mandate this ordering, but it is a defensible implementation choice; no observed success or effectiveness guarantee is inferred.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Every observation should be evaluated against every explanation, including combined explanations, with consistency, inconsistency, or indeterminacy recorded alongside reasons and confidence.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The proposed comparison directly instantiates S002's requirement to evaluate each evidence item against all competing explanations. Including combinations fits the target's explicit possibility of multiple contributors. Recording inconsistency, consistency, indeterminacy, reasons and confidence provides a relevant comparative assessment without forcing uncertain observations into definite judgments. Unspecified classification criteria and confidence scales limit reproducibility but do not defeat this proposed operation's license. This judgment establishes neither successful execution nor causal identification.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Reliable contradictions should take priority over counts of supporting observations when comparing explanations.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: This comparative priority faithfully implements the source's emphasis on inconsistency and diagnostic importance rather than simple supporting counts. It is relevant to distinguishing the target's multiple plausible causes despite incomplete and differing measurements. Within this methodological scope, no numerical weighting rule is required; reliability, diagnosticity and sensitivity still govern interpretation. This licenses the proposed comparison without establishing that any contradiction or causal finding has been observed.

obligation_verdicts.subject: The comparison should be repeated after excluding unreliable readings and varying uncertain handoff times and sensor-response assumptions.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The proposed repetition directly instantiates S002's sensitivity testing of uncertain evidence and assumptions. Reading reliability, handoff timing and sensor response bear on distinguishing warming stages from measurement differences in this target. Comparing results under these changes can reveal whether explanatory rankings depend on uncertain inputs. Exclusion criteria and variation ranges remain implementation details to specify; no completed assessment, stable ranking or causal finding is established.

obligation_verdicts.subject: If a device or procedure compromises food handling, its use should stop, and any redeployment must be safe.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule prospectively links a handling-compromise trigger to a definite response: stop using the implicated device or procedure, with safe use required for any redeployment. The continuing normal food-handling requirements provide a reference standard sufficient for this investigation-level control rule, despite the absence of detailed operational thresholds. Stopping and conditional redeployment are internally coherent. This judgment does not establish that a compromise occurred or that any redeployment is safe.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Failed or missing traces should be treated as inconclusive.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: S005 identifies unreliable evidence as a source of misleading comparisons. Missing or failed monitoring records provide no reliable temperature history with which to discriminate among explanations, justifying inconclusive treatment of those records. This limitation does not imply that other reliable evidence or usable portions of a trace are inconclusive, and it does not assert that monitoring failures have occurred.

obligation_verdicts.subject: If a reliable, package-relevant rise occurs before loading and transit readings are subsequently stable, that pattern would contradict transit as the sole origin for the monitored package.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Under the stated measurement conditions, warming located before loading is inconsistent with transit being its sole origin for that package. This licenses the source mechanism's use of reliable inconsistency to weaken an explanation. The consequence remains hypothetical and package-specific; it neither establishes that the pattern occurred nor excludes transit as a contributor or proves another explanation. Unspecified measurement thresholds limit practical application but do not defeat the stated conditional relation.

obligation_verdicts.subject: If conditions remain acceptable through departure and a rise then occurs in transit, that pattern would weaken a solely preloading explanation.
unresolved_conditions: “Acceptable conditions” must establish relevant package temperatures through departure, rather than merely acceptable surrounding air.
The transit rise must represent meaningful package warming rather than measurement uncertainty or delayed sensor response.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The transferred mechanism licenses weakening an explanation when reliable evidence is inconsistent with it. Under these conditions, the hypothetical pattern would weaken a solely preloading explanation within the monitored case. However, the unspecified referent of acceptable conditions and threshold for a rise leave its diagnostic relevance unresolved. The pattern is not established as observed and would not prove a transit cause or exclude preloading contributions.

obligation_verdicts.subject: If conditions remain acceptable through arrival and warming then occurs during a documented receiving delay, that pattern would weaken explanations confined to earlier stages.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Under the stated temporal-resolution, sensor-placement and measurement-comparability conditions, warming localized after arrival would count against explanations confined to earlier stages in the monitored case. This licenses weakening, without eliminating earlier contributions, excluding combined mechanisms or proving that the delay caused warming. The relation remains hypothetical and establishes neither an observed outcome nor food-safety status.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Disagreement between usual and standardized readings would support investigating measurement differences.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Under the stated pairing and comparability requirements, disagreement would give a defensible reason to investigate measurement differences, consistent with comparing explanations through potentially discriminating evidence. The target already identifies differing receiving methods. An unspecified disagreement threshold limits evidential weight but does not defeat this modest investigative consequence. The relation neither establishes measurement error as the cause nor assumes disagreement has occurred.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Agreement between usual and standardized readings on elevated package temperature would weaken measurement differences as the sole explanation.
unresolved_conditions: The standardized measurement must provide a sufficiently reliable reference, with shared measurement errors assessed so that agreement is diagnostically meaningful.
Agreement and elevation must be distinguishable within the measurements' uncertainty.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The mechanism licenses weakening an explanation when evidence meaningfully conflicts with it. Comparable readings agreeing on elevation could weaken a measurement-only explanation, but temporal alignment, placement and comparability alone do not establish accuracy: shared error could produce the same agreement. The relation is therefore licensed subject to the unresolved reliability conditions, without asserting that agreement has occurred or locating a warming stage.

obligation_verdicts.subject: The proposed signal comparisons require adequate temporal resolution, suitable sensor placement, and comparable measurements; otherwise the evidence should be marked indeterminate.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The target's intermittent bay records, missing package tracking, and differing receiving methods justify this interpretability limit. Insufficient temporal resolution can obscure which stage contains a temperature change; unsuitable placement can measure conditions unrelated to the package; incomparable measurements can produce apparent differences unrelated to warming. These mechanisms align with the source's warning about unreliable evidence and mistaken diagnosticity. Marking the affected comparison indeterminate is warranted. Operational thresholds remain unspecified, but that does not undermine the qualitative limitation or establish that any proposed measurement actually fails it.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Multiple rises could support combined contributors.
unresolved_conditions: The hypothetical rises must provide diagnostic timing or other information favoring combined contributors over a single recurring mechanism or measurement artifacts; measurement interpretability alone does not establish this.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The transferred mechanism licenses support through discriminating comparisons among explanations. Multiple interpretable rises could favor combined contributors, but their number alone does not distinguish multiple contributors from repeated effects of one mechanism. The required diagnostic pattern is unspecified. No rises or combined causes are treated as observed or proven.

obligation_verdicts.subject: None of the proposed diagnostic observations is yet established.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: P024 repeats the assertion without independently establishing it. T001 describes limited existing records and unresolved causes, but does not provide a complete account establishing that none of the proposed diagnostic observations was established at mapping time. The assertion is neither independently confirmed nor contradicted.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Explanations should be weakened in proportion to the importance and reliability of their contradictions.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: S004 warrants greater weakening for important inconsistencies, while S005 establishes that unreliable evidence and mistaken diagnosticity can undermine that assessment. Together they support the stated qualitative weighting principle, without establishing a numerical proportionality rule. The claim prescribes how to update assessments; it does not assert that any contradiction has been observed or any particular explanation weakened.

obligation_verdicts.subject: An explanation may be eliminated only within the scope actually tested.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: S004 grounds elimination in important inconsistencies with observed evidence, while S005 identifies limitations that can undermine those comparisons. T001 describes incomplete package tracking, limited monitoring capacity and differing delivery and receiving conditions. These justify restricting elimination to the cases and explanatory scope tested: a contradiction for one package or circumstance does not exclude that mechanism elsewhere. This restriction does not assert that any explanation has been eliminated or that testing alone suffices for elimination.

obligation_verdicts.subject: The next investigation should focus on surviving alternatives and observations that would distinguish them.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: As a principle for selecting follow-up investigation after comparison, this faithfully extends the mechanism: important inconsistencies weaken alternatives, and diagnostic observations distinguish those remaining. This directly serves the manager's need to investigate unresolved causes with limited observations. No particular surviving alternative, successful measurement, or causal conclusion is asserted. A rule optimizing the choice among observations is unnecessary for this scoped recommendation; surviving alternatives remain provisional.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Existing cold-staging practices should be reinforced during the fortnight.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Reinforcing cold-staging practices is relevant to interim handling, but this ordinary control action does not instantiate the transferred mechanism of comparing competing explanations, prioritizing contradictions, and testing sensitivity. The proposal specifies neither a diagnostic comparison nor comparative evidence selecting staging for intervention. Its practical relevance alone does not satisfy this contract; this judgment does not establish that reinforcing existing practices is inappropriate.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Existing cold-staging practices
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 establishes refrigerated operations, loading-bay temperature logs and continuing food-handling requirements, but does not establish existing cold-staging practices available to reinforce. P027 proposes reinforcing such practices; that proposal cannot substantiate its own factual presupposition. The assertion therefore requires an unstated inference, although the practices' absence is not established either.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Avoidable unprotected handoff delays should be reduced during the fortnight.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Reducing unprotected delays is relevant as an interim handling precaution, but the proposed action does not instantiate the transferred mechanism: comparing evidence across competing explanations, prioritizing contradictions, and testing sensitivity. The proposal specifies neither a diagnostic comparison nor a connection to results of that comparison. Its practical relevance does not satisfy the mechanism-fidelity requirement. This judgment does not establish that reducing delays is inappropriate or that delays caused the exceptions.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Approved receiving measurements should be standardized where feasible during the fortnight.
unresolved_conditions: The selected approved protocol must provide reliable, comparable readings within the available staff capacity and food-handling requirements; its specification and feasibility remain unresolved.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Receiving methods differ across sites, so standardization is relevant to reducing measurement uncertainty in the comparison of competing explanations. This supports the transferred mechanism's need for reliable evidence, provided the chosen standard actually makes readings comparable. Approval and uniformity alone do not establish reliability or diagnostic value. No improved measurements or causal findings are established.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Credible stage-specific evidence should be used to target additional temporary supervision or handling changes at that stage.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule prospectively links an identifiable trigger—available credible evidence specific to a stage—to a prescribed response: direct additional temporary supervision or handling changes to that stage. This is sufficiently determinate and internally coherent at the stated targeting scope, although it leaves the particular intervention to discretion. This judgment does not establish evidence credibility or intervention effectiveness.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Additional temporary supervision or handling changes
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Targeting action using credible stage-specific evidence is relevant to the manager's decision. However, the particular intervention is unspecified, so its mechanism, feasibility and conformity with food-handling requirements cannot be assessed. The transferred mechanism supports comparing and weakening explanations; it does not itself establish that an unspecified intervention is appropriate or effective. The proposal supplies neither an assessable intervention nor observed stage-specific findings.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Whenever a reading triggers existing food-handling or disposition requirements, those requirements must be applied without waiting for causal certainty or relaxing them.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule specifies a prospective trigger—activation of existing requirements by a reading—and a prescribed response—apply those requirements without causal-certainty delays or relaxation. Incorporating existing requirements makes the trigger and response sufficiently determinate at this scope without restating their thresholds. The decision structure is internally coherent and asserts no observed compliance or effectiveness.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Temporary controls that remain justified should be retained at the fortnight's end.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule is prospective and internally coherent, with a clear review time and prescribed response: retain qualifying controls. However, 'remain justified' supplies no criteria for deciding which controls qualify. The trigger therefore leaves the central continuation decision unspecified and is insufficiently determinate at the stated scope. This judgment concerns decision structure alone.

obligation_verdicts.subject: If the ranking remains unstable or coverage is inadequate at the fortnight's end, a focused next sampling round should be specified.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule specifies a review time, two alternative triggers, and a prescribed response: specify a focused follow-up sampling round. Sensitivity comparisons and recorded coverage gaps give the qualitative triggers sufficient meaning at this planning scope. The next round's detailed design is the required output, so its absence does not make the rule incoherent. This judgment establishes neither that either trigger has occurred nor that further sampling will be informative or effective.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Specify a focused next sampling round
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Further sampling could inform the competing explanations, but the proposed round specifies neither allocation nor measurements. Its trigger alone does not establish that it would obtain discriminating evidence, support comparison and sensitivity testing, or be feasible beyond the authorized two-week observation period. The proposal therefore lacks enough detail to determine whether this substantive operation instantiates the transferred mechanism.

obligation_verdicts.subject: If the ranking remains unstable or coverage is inadequate at the fortnight's end, a cause should not be declared.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Unstable comparisons or inadequate coverage leave causal attribution insufficiently supported given multiple possible contributors, limited monitoring, and differing receiving methods. The source mechanism requires sensitivity assessment and warns that surviving explanations are not thereby proven. These justify withholding a causal declaration under either stated condition, without asserting that either condition has occurred or that stability and adequate coverage would suffice to establish causation.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Sparse, selectively monitored packages cannot establish prevalence.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The target includes heterogeneous bays, carriers, routes and receiving methods, with limited monitoring capacity. The proposed selective monitoring supplies no representative sampling design or justified population weighting. Frequencies among monitored packages therefore cannot establish population prevalence. This limitation concerns the proposed design; sparse samples can support prevalence estimates under suitable sampling assumptions.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Sparse, selectively monitored packages cannot clear an entire delivery, carrier, bay, or route.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The target establishes limited monitoring capacity, untracked package histories, and varied operating and receiving conditions. Findings from selected packages therefore lack a warranted bridge to blanket exoneration of any listed larger unit: unmonitored packages and occasions remain unresolved. This justifies the stated generalization limit without asserting that any unmonitored package actually experienced warming.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Air traces, sensor lag, clock errors, device error, package variability, and different measurement locations can create misleading apparent contradictions.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: S005 supports the risk that unreliable evidence misleads comparisons. T001 makes measurement comparability relevant: room logs, single-package readings, and differing receiving methods measure different aspects of deliveries. Air and package temperatures can differ; sensor lag and clock errors can misplace changes in time; device error, package variability, and measurement location can produce discrepancies unrelated to an explanation's truth. These mechanisms justify the modest 'can' limitation without establishing that any distortion occurred or its magnitude.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Repeated readings and records from one delivery are not independent confirmations and should be treated as dependent in the comparison.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Readings and records within one delivery share its handling and thermal history, so counting them as independent confirmations would overstate replication. This target structure supports accounting for within-delivery dependence, including in sensitivity assessment. S005 identifies dependent evidence as a source of misleading comparisons, and S002 warrants testing uncertain assumptions. The limitation does not require perfect dependence or imply that repeated readings provide no additional information; the degree of dependence remains unspecified.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Sensitivity to missing mechanisms, subjective consistency judgments, mistaken diagnosticity, or shared assumptions requires an explicitly uncertain conclusion.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule prospectively connects an identifiable qualitative trigger—comparison sensitivity to the listed limitations—to a clear response: explicitly express uncertainty in the conclusion. Although no sensitivity threshold is specified, the trigger and response are sufficiently determinate for this limited reporting scope and internally coherent. This assesses the proposed rule's structure without asserting that sensitivity has been observed.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Sensitivity to missing mechanisms, subjective consistency judgments, mistaken diagnosticity, or shared assumptions requires revised hypotheses or measurements.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The proposition is prospective and internally coherent, but its decision structure is insufficiently determinate. It does not specify what sensitivity triggers revision, which hypotheses or measurements require revision, or how to choose between those responses. The instruction to test sensitivity supplies no missing selection criteria. This judgment concerns only the rule's structure, not the value or effectiveness of revision.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Revise hypotheses or measurements
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Sensitivity testing and the listed limitations justify reconsidering the comparison, but no particular hypothesis or measurement revision is specified. The packet therefore does not establish whether the proposed transformation preserves comparison against competing explanations, improves discrimination among possible delivery-stage causes, or fits the target's operational constraints. P034 states the proposal; it does not demonstrate those properties.

obligation_verdicts.subject: An internal-range exception alone does not establish food-safety status.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 specifies an internal receiving range without establishing its relationship to food-safety criteria. A single package reading, differing receiving methods, and incomplete temperature histories do not supply that missing relationship. The exception alone therefore warrants neither a safe nor an unsafe classification; this limitation does not suspend existing food-handling requirements.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Improvement after a temporary change does not by itself establish causation.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Temporal improvement alone does not distinguish an intervention effect from other contributors, ordinary variation, or measurement differences. The target permits multiple contributors and differing receiving measurements, so improvement could fit several explanations. S006 reinforces the distinction between an explanation remaining compatible with evidence and being established as true. This justifies the limited 'by itself' restriction without asserting that improvement or any confound actually occurred.

ablation.policy: Simultaneous deletion of frozen semantic claim objects under H7. Source/target facts unchanged. CONTEXT spans are attribution only; no deleted premise may be reused. Conditional/uncertain claims retained with flags.
